summary: Assessed 8 claim(s); found 19 failure mode(s); 2 claim(s) below the 0.70 confidence threshold.

claims.text: The float verification defect is reader-side: serde_json's default decimal-to-f64 parsing is not correctly rounded, so for a class of payload floats the verifier recomputes a canonical body from bits 1 ULP away from the bits hashed at append, and reports hash-mismatch on an untampered log.
boundary: Scope: verification path (read_events + verify_events) in crates/axiomere and its bindings
The writer (canonical rendering) is not implicated: the stored text is the correct shortest form of the appended value

evidence.ref: Reproduction 2026-10-12: append {"ts_like": 1791810119.6349843} via Python package -> verify() false in-session, Database.open raises 'verification failed at seq 1: hash-mismatch'; frozen as crates/axiomere/tests/fixtures/legacy-floats-defect.axmr

Primitive probe (probe results recorded in spec §2): serde_json parses text 1791810119.6349843 to bits 0x41dab33691e8a396; correctly-rounded parse (Python) gives 0x41dab33691e8a395, whose serde_json rendering is the same text
Tekmerion finding, src/tekmerion/platform/ledger.py payload-discipline note (2026-10-12): same failure observed downstream with the same value

falsification_tests: F-FLT-1: exhibit the failure with a correctly-rounded parser substituted for serde_json's default while holding the stored bytes fixed — if it still fails, the defect is not reader-side parsing.

claims.text: The trigger class is payload floats whose canonical decimal needs at least 17 significant digits (including exponent forms); the parse error is always exactly 1 ULP; decimals of at most 16 significant digits are unaffected.
boundary: Rates measured on random bit patterns and timestamp-shaped decimals; the class boundary (17 significant digits) is the invariant, the percentages are sample statistics

evidence.ref: Bit-pattern sweep: 593,459 / 2,000,000 random finite f64 fail format->parse round trip under the default parser (spec §2)

Shape sweep: timestamp-shaped decimals (10 integer digits + k fraction digits), 200,000 trials per k: 0 unstable at k<=6 (<=16 significant digits), ~5% at k=7 (17 significant), ~12% at k>=9; all mismatches +-1 ULP

falsification_tests: F-FLT-2: a float with a canonical form of at most 16 significant digits that fails the pre-fix round trip, or a pre-fix parse error of 2+ ULP.
